items.title: Microsoft corrects Copilot Business nonprofit pricing in the December price-list preview
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed that the December price-list preview had incorrect pricing for the Microsoft 365 Copilot Business nonprofit offer, and says the corrected preview was republished on November 9. Partners who accessed the earlier version are advised to download the updated price list; the notice does not specify the corrected amount.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 begins rolling out in Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio
items.summary: Microsoft is adding Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 as a model choice in Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio, expanding the models available for complex work. Microsoft says Work IQ can ground its responses in organizational files, meetings, chats, and business data within existing permissions; the rollout is for eligible users.

items.title: Azure Content Understanding добавляет поддержку GPT-5.6, GPT-6 и GPT-6.1
items.summary: Azure Content Understanding добавил поддержку семейств GPT-5.6, GPT-6 и GPT-6.1 для обработки документов, текста, речи и видео. Расширение каталога позволяет подбирать модели под конкретные задачи и компромисс между качеством и стоимостью.

items.title: Microsoft details two-phase NTLM signing security improvements for Windows
items.summary: Microsoft says Windows updates from November 10, 2026, begin the first phase of NTLM signing improvements addressing CVE-2026-118737: clients offer signing by default on non-anonymous connections, with auditing to identify connections not using it. A second phase planned for May 2027 will make Windows servers require signing by default, giving administrators a timeline to assess compatibility and prepare.

items.title: Bring Your Own Model becomes generally available in Visual Studio
items.summary: Bring Your Own Model is now generally available in Visual Studio 18.12, allowing developers to use provider, self-hosted, or local models without leaving the IDE. The release adds multiple named configurations, custom endpoints and local-model support, API-format controls, and improved proxy handling; GitHub sign-in is not required.

items.title: GitHub makes issue types and fields available for personal accounts
items.summary: GitHub made issue types and issue fields generally available for repositories owned by personal accounts, bringing customizable planning features to individual developers and open-source maintainers. Users can configure up to 25 types and 25 fields and manage them through projects, APIs, and webhooks.

items.title: Anthropic’s updated Usage Policy takes effect, clarifying high-risk use and regional eligibility
items.summary: Anthropic’s updated Usage Policy took effect November 12. The update clarifies requirements for high-risk health and finance use, adds controls for autonomous physical actions, addresses abusive behavior toward models, and clarifies that supported-region restrictions also apply based on an organization’s incorporation, headquarters, ownership, or control.

items.title: Anthropic opens self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta
items.summary: Anthropic introduced a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, allowing developers to run the service and store agent credentials and session history in their own cloud or on-premises environment. Organizations can choose where model requests are routed, including Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google’s Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or their own gateway.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Claude for Manufacturing with 17 skills and four connectors
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin with 17 skills for tasks such as quoting, quality investigations, troubleshooting, sourcing, design comparisons, and production reporting. It connects to Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365, and Oracle NetSuite; Anthropic says it is for Team and Enterprise plans, keeps people in review of the work, and does not operate equipment.

items.title: OpenAI pledges $2 million for research on AI and children’s safety
items.summary: OpenAI says it signed a charter on safer AI for children and committed $2 million to support a global research network studying AI’s effects on children. The funding will support shared measurement tools for assessing risks and opportunities, with research intended to inform safer products and policy.

items.title: OpenAI partners with Aleph to expand ChatGPT Ads into 44 countries
items.summary: OpenAI is expanding the reach of ChatGPT Ads into 44 countries through an exclusive reseller agreement with Aleph. Aleph will provide local support for brands and agencies across several regions, extending OpenAI’s advertising presence beyond its existing markets.

items.title: Gemini Live launches on Apple CarPlay
items.summary: Google brought Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay, enabling hands-free conversations while driving, including tasks such as summarizing emails and checking a calendar. The global rollout began November 11 for Gemini users on iOS in supported Gemini Live languages.

items.title: Google launches Gemini Decisions API and Gemini Decision 1
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini Decision 1 and the Gemini Decisions API for fast, closed-set decisions across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. It supports up to 1,000 questions per request, returns probabilities and confidence scores, and is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens with no charge for output tokens.

items.title: Google DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2 for cell-specific DNA predictions
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a model designed to predict how genetic variants affect specific human cell types and states. The company reports nearly twice as many identified causal variants on a benchmark compared with its prior state of the art; the model is available for non-commercial research and in a commercial-research preview.

items.title: Databricks plans roughly $3 billion investment across Europe and the Middle East
items.summary: Databricks announced plans to invest about $3 billion across Europe and the Middle East, expanding regional teams and supporting adoption of its AI and agent products. The investment could deepen its enterprise presence and capacity to help regional customers build and scale AI systems.

items.title: Salesforce releases autonomous R&D agents that improve AI models
items.summary: Salesforce introduced SFR-AutoR&D, a system of agents designed to carry out research loops, improve codebases, and train models. Salesforce reports that its use on EmbeddingGemma 2 produced a new embedding model with better quality and latency, illustrating a potential route to automated enterprise model improvement.

items.title: Sompo Holdings and NTT partner to explore physical AI in nursing care
items.summary: Sompo Holdings and NTT agreed to study real-world physical-AI deployment in Japan’s nursing-care sector, with labor shortages as a key motivation. Initial potential use cases include support tasks such as cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and moving items, while the companies assess pathways from demonstrations to commercialization.

items.title: MIT researchers develop a more data-efficient method for climate AI models
items.summary: MIT researchers reported a method for training climate-emulation AI with a smaller, carefully optimized synthetic dataset. Their report says the resulting models were more adaptable to scenarios not seen in training, potentially making useful climate tools faster to produce and update.

items.title: European Commission issues guidance on AI Act transparency obligations
items.summary: The European Commission published guidance on implementing the AI Act’s Article 50 transparency obligations for certain AI systems. The guidance provides an implementation reference for organizations subject to the Act’s AI transparency requirements.

items.title: Kindo raises $30 million to expand enterprise AI-agent controls
items.summary: Kindo announced a $30 million financing expansion, bringing its total capital raised to $57.6 million. It plans to expand go-to-market operations and develop its platform for discovering, monitoring, and governing enterprise AI-agent activity.
